platform.windows: compiles; the Windows session path is T6 and no Windows QUIC run has been recorded
platform.note: The CONNECT-IP peers are loopback HTTP/3 servers on macOS arm64. Nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run.

shape: private-key is base64 of a SEC1 ECPrivateKey (x509.ParseECPrivateKey); public-key is base64 of a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo (x509.ParsePKIXPublicKey) asserted to be ECDSA; both are P-256 in every WARP registration

the client certificate is generated with x509.CreateCertificate from a zero template: serial 0, empty issuer/subject, one-day validity; the endpoint certificate is accepted by pinning its public key (InsecureSkipVerify + VerifyConnection), so certificate names are not verified
SNI defaults to consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com and uri to https://cloudflareaccess.com; a URI template with variables is refused ('IP flow forwarding not supported')
QUIC with datagrams (InitialPacketSize 1242, keepalive 30 s); HTTP/3 SETTINGS additionally sends the draft-00 datagram identifier 0x276; the peer must advertise extended CONNECT and datagrams
:protocol cf-connect-ip, :scheme https, :authority/:path from uri, capsule-protocol ?1, empty user-agent
ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255 and ::-all-ones with protocol 0; ADDRESS_ASSIGN/ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT parsed from the request stream; ADDRESS_REQUEST is an error in connect-ip-go
IP packets are sent in QUIC DATAGRAM frames (quarter stream ID + context ID 0 + packet) and terminated in mipstack or gVisor, which is what serves TCP and UDP
mtu defaults to 1280; ip/ipv6 default to a /32 and /128 host prefix

implementedSubset.protocol: RFC 9484 CONNECT-IP over HTTP/3 (RFC 9114) with HTTP Datagrams (RFC 9297), the capsule protocol and extended CONNECT (RFC 9220), for UDP; RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP from T14 is unchanged
files: native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel/src/outbound/masque_ip.rs (CONNECT-IP: request, capsules, IP packets, flows, tunnel DNS)
native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel/src/outbound/warp.rs (SEC1/PKCS#8 key parsing, client certificate, SPKI pin, TLS config)
native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel/src/outbound/quic.rs (connect_with_tls_config for the WARP client certificate and pin)
native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel-cli/tests/cli.rs (process loads the WARP shape, TCP refused)
native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel-cli/tests/family_cli.rs (SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE through a CONNECT-IP peer)
wireBehaviour: one QUIC connection per UDP association, ALPN h3, keep-alive 30 s, T10 transport windows, datagram receive/send buffers 64 KiB each

client SETTINGS: ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL (0x08), H3_DATAGRAM (0x33) and the draft-00 identifier (0x276); the peer must advertise extended CONNECT and at least one datagram setting, otherwise the association fails with a named error before opening a request

request: :method CONNECT, :protocol cf-connect-ip, :scheme https, :authority/:path from uri (default https://cloudflareaccess.com), capsule-protocol ?1, empty user-agent; 2xx plus capsule-protocol ?1 required

TLS: the client certificate is generated from the configured P-256 key (serial 0, empty names, one day, ecdsa-with-SHA256); the endpoint certificate is accepted only when its SubjectPublicKeyInfo equals public-key (skip-cert-verify drops the pin); neither the chain nor the name is verified, matching the pinned adapter

ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT (0x03) with the pinned IPv4 and IPv6 full ranges and protocol 0 is sent after the 2xx; the peer's ADDRESS_ASSIGN (0x01) and ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT are parsed and exposed; ADDRESS_REQUEST (0x02) fails the association by name

IP packets: IPv4 with 20-byte headers (DF set, header checksum, fragments refused) or IPv6 with 40-byte headers (extension headers refused); UDP checksum verified and always computed; TTL/hop limit 64; payload bounded by mtu (default 1280: 1252 bytes over IPv4, 1232 over IPv6). A packet larger than what one QUIC datagram frame of the current path can carry is a named error (TooLarge), not a silent drop or a synthesised ICMP

sending: one QUIC DATAGRAM frame per packet with quarter stream ID + context ID 0 + packet; receiving: the same frames, plus DATAGRAM capsules (0x00) on the request stream; datagrams for another quarter stream or context are ignored

UDP flows: one local source port per destination (40000-65535), at most 32 per association, least-recently-used eviction; a reply is delivered only when its destination address/port and source address match the flow

remote-dns-resolve + dns: an A then AAAA UDP query to each configured name server through the tunnel, with a bounded pending queue for other datagrams received during the lookup; without it, the host resolves locally before the packet is built

the client does not send ADDRESS_REQUEST: the pinned adapter relies on the configured ip/ipv6 prefixes and the server's ADDRESS_ASSIGN (WARP assigns the addresses itself); an address request from the peer is refused
T21 extends the same tunnel with a minimal TCP client (outbound/tcp.rs) for `dial`; the UDP flow table and the datagram framing are unchanged
acceptedOptions: name-cert-verify (no-op, as in the pinned adapter)
rejectedAtLoad: congestion-controller / cwnd / bbr-profile (QUIC controller: quinn has no equivalent)
dialer-proxy (a QUIC endpoint is dialled locally)
dns entries that are not udp:// IP literals (TCP/DoT/DoH, #params)
a CONNECT-IP shape without private-key/public-key or without ip/ipv6
rejectedAtDial: TCP over the RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset: RFC 9298 carries UDP only, so a TCP dial configured with that shape is refused by name (the CONNECT-IP/WARP shape gained TCP termination in T21)
notImplemented: ICMP: incoming ICMP is reported/dropped, no ICMP error is synthesised for a datagram that does not fit the QUIC datagram limit
IPv4 options, IPv4 reassembly, IPv6 extension headers
IP flow forwarding / URI templates, and assigning addresses to the peer (ADDRESS_REQUEST)
DNS over TCP/DoT/DoH name servers and DNS name servers named by hostname
capsule-carried datagrams for sending (the pinned adapter sends QUIC datagram frames)
DATA frames larger than 2 KiB, capsules larger than 1536 bytes and more than 32 flows per association (local bounds)
TCP over CONNECT-IP was added by T21 (outbound/tcp.rs); this file records the UDP/IP data path it builds on

minimalIpStack.ipv4: 20-byte headers, total-length and header-checksum validation, DF set on built packets, fragments refused, protocol other than UDP reported
minimalIpStack.ipv6: 40-byte headers, payload-length validation, next header must be UDP (or ICMPv6, reported), no extension-header walk
minimalIpStack.udp: length validation, checksum verified when present (mandatory over IPv6) and always computed; pseudo-header per family; zero checksum sent as 0xffff over IPv6
minimalIpStack.independentVectors: the IPv4 packet vector in ipstack.rs::tests::ipv4_udp_packet_matches_an_independent_vector and the IPv6 UDP checksum (0x8a77) were computed with a separate Python RFC 1071 implementation: checksum(b) = ~fold(sum16(b)) over the header (checksum field zero), UDP checksum over src||dst||0x0011||len||udp (IPv4) or src||dst||len32||0x00000011||udp (IPv6); the CONNECT-IP peer in tests/quic_peers.rs uses its own IP/UDP codec again, so one implementation cannot mask the other's bug

memory.budget: T7 verifies 40,000,000 bytes (decimal) for the whole iOS VPN extension (R3)
perAssociation: QUIC: stream receive window 512 KiB + connection receive 2 MiB + send window 2 MiB = 4,718,592 B
QUIC datagram receive 64 KiB + send 64 KiB = 131,072 B
request stream: one 2 KiB DATA frame + a 3 KiB capsule buffer + one packet copy (~MTU) = ~6.4 KB
inbound packet queue: 4 x up to 65,535 B = 262,140 B (quinn's datagram receive buffer bounds one datagram below 64 KiB)
flow table: 32 flows + a port index (~8 KB with Target strings)
pending datagrams during a tunnel-DNS lookup: 8 x MTU = 10,240 B
key material, certificate and verifier state: < 4 KB
memory.note: About 5.2 MB decimal per CONNECT-IP association (CONNECT-UDP remains ~19 MB, recorded in t14-feasibility.json). The engine creates one association per SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE and Limits.max_sessions defaults to 256, so T7/T6 must cap concurrent masque associations (or lower max_sessions). Dropping the association closes the QUIC connection and both reader tasks end (their channel sends fail); no pool exists.
memory.notMeasured: no device RSS: the numbers are analytic bounds from the configured windows and buffers, not a measurement on an iPhone

controlledPeer.what: a quinn HTTP/3 server that requires the client certificate (recording its SubjectPublicKeyInfo), advertises 0x08/0x33/0x276, answers `cf-connect-ip`, reads the ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT, assigns 172.16.0.2/32 and fd00::2/128, and echoes tunnelled IP/UDP packets with its own IPv4/IPv6/UDP codec (header and UDP checksums validated, DNS A answers for tunnel-resolved names); modes: no datagram settings, ADDRESS_REQUEST, 403 refusal
controlledPeer.whyNotPinnedMihomo: the pinned masque adapter is a client for Cloudflare WARP with no `listeners:` mode and an endpoint that is not reachable offline, so no pinned-binary interop is claimed

optionMatrix.result: 250 no-op cases / 270 enabled cases, 0 problems; masque is no longer skipped: its WARP base carries a throwaway P-256 key pair and local address, every no-op form is accepted by both engines, and the rejected modes (h2, h3-l4proxy, gvisor stack, QUIC congestion knobs, dialer-proxy) are named
optionMatrix.note: the enabled `dialer-proxy` row is rejected by both engines (Mihomo rejects it for masque too)

decisionsForT9: masque is still partial after T18 and T21: the WARP shape serves UDP and TCP over CONNECT-IP, but `network: h2`, `network: h3-l4proxy`, ip-stack.mode gvisor and the QUIC congestion knobs stay rejected, passive/simultaneous-open TCP and window scaling/SACK/timestamps are not implemented, and the pinned binary's exact TCP stack (mipstack/gVisor) is not reproduced. Do not count masque as fully compatible.
CONNECT-IP reuses the T14 HTTP/3 client; the new SETTINGS value 0x276 is parsed in the same place, so a future HTTP/3 feature does not need a second client.

A WARP registration is not required for the configuration to load: the key pair and endpoint pin are parsed and used, and the certificate is generated locally. Only an actual WARP endpoint is missing offline, which is why the peer is controlled.
decisionsForT7: Cap concurrent masque associations: one CONNECT-IP association is ~5.2 MB decimal analytic worst case (CONNECT-UDP ~19 MB); with the 40,000,000-byte extension budget, a few concurrent associations plus the rest of the extension must be measured and bounded.
The CONNECT-IP association closes its QUIC connection when dropped; both reader tasks end on the closed channel/connection, and no flow state outlives the association.
iOS Network Extension build: no new dependency was added (ring, rustls, quinn and bytes were already used); there is no C library and no Go code in the binary.
license: No GPL-3.0 source is vendored, linked, copied or translated. The client is written from RFC 9484/9298/9297/9220/9114; the pinned `adapter/outbound/masque.go` and `transport/masque` (GPL-3.0) were read only to record which option names, defaults and capsule flows the pinned binary accepts (the same compatibility exercise as the option tables in proxies.rs), and the implementation here is independent: the DER/base64/calendar helpers are written from the encoding rules, the IPv4/IPv6/UDP codec from RFC 791/8200/768, and the ECDSA signature/verification uses `ring` (already the TLS provider). The QPACK static table and Huffman table in src/outbound/h3.rs remain the MIT metacubex/qpack and BSD-3-Clause x/net tables recorded in native-kernel/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; T18 added no third-party material and no new dependency.
